properties.natural_language: Data received at boundary edge EDGE-EL-PAYLOAD-VALIDATION must be validated for correct format and type before processing.
Inputs crossing trust boundary at EDGE-EL-PAYLOAD-VALIDATION must be checked for cryptographic validity where applicable.
Data received at boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-ATTESTATION must be validated for correct format and type before processing.
Inputs crossing trust boundary at EDGE-RECEIVE-ATTESTATION must be checked for cryptographic validity where applicable.

The ambiguity 'The specification states credential changes are 'irreversible once on-chain' but does not explicitly define the behavior if a duplicate BLSToExecutionChange with a different target address is submitted.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The assumption 'The execution engine is trusted to honor the withdrawals specified in PayloadAttributes and include them in the produced execution payload.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Validator operators are assumed to securely store their BLS withdrawal keys separately from signing keys.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
Once a validator's withdrawal credentials are changed from BLS (0x00) to execution (0x01), the change is irreversible.
The execution engine must be trusted to include all specified withdrawals in the execution payload without omission or reordering.
BLS withdrawal keys used for credential changes must not be derivable from validator signing keys.
The ambiguity 'The LightClientStore upgrade MAY be performed before ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'No explicit description of what happens if a merkle branch is already at or exceeds the required Electra depth' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The assumption 'The generalized indices used for Electra are correct and correspond to the actual SSZ tree structure of Electra beacon state' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.

The assumption 'All nodes will eventually upgrade to Electra and the network format for pre-fork data will remain available during the transition period' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
LightClientStore upgrade to Electra format must only be performed when the store's data is consistent and valid.
After upgrading LightClientStore to Electra, all Merkle branches must have the correct depth for the new SSZ structure.
Pre-fork light client data must remain accessible and verifiable after the Electra upgrade.
Data received at boundary edge EDGE-PEER-BLOCK-FORK must be validated for correct format and type before processing.
Inputs crossing trust boundary at EDGE-PEER-BLOCK-FORK must be checked for cryptographic validity where applicable.

The ambiguity 'The specification does not define behavior when an unknown identity scheme is encountered' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'The phrase 'endpoint information is not required' is ambiguous - unclear if records without endpoints should be propagated or only stored locally' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'No specification for how sequence numbers should increment or what constitutes a 'newer' record beyond simple comparison' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The assumption 'The secp256k1 elliptic curve and keccak256 hash function are cryptographically secure' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'An attacker cannot recover the private key from the public key in the ENR or from multiple signatures' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'DNS infrastructure used for ENR discovery provides authentic responses (DNSSEC or trusted resolver)' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Nodes properly increment sequence numbers when updating their ENR' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
ENR records must have a valid signature under the declared identity scheme before being accepted.
ENR records must not exceed the 300-byte RLP size limit.
After updating an ENR, the sequence number must be strictly greater than the previous record's sequence number.
An attacker must not be able to forge or modify ENR records without the node's private key.

The ambiguity 'The specification does not define what new consensus behavior EIP-7805 introduces beyond the fork version change. The fork logic is purely mechanical state upgrade.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'EIP7805_FORK_EPOCH is set to the maximum uint64 value (18446744073709551615), marked as TBD.' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The assumption 'All validator client implementations will correctly implement the upgrade_to_eip7805 function, producing identical post-fork state roots.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'The Fulu fork has been successfully activated before EIP-7805, as this fork upgrades from Fulu state.' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The Fulu fork must be fully activated before the EIP-7805 upgrade function is invoked.
The EIP7805_FORK_VERSION must be distinct from all other fork versions to prevent version collision.
Data received at boundary edge EDGE-BLOCK-PROPOSER-INCLUSION must be validated for correct format and type before processing.
Inputs crossing trust boundary at EDGE-BLOCK-PROPOSER-INCLUSION must be checked for cryptographic validity where applicable.

The ambiguity 'The specification does not define how USER_CONFIGURED_MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK is specified in configuration files' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'The relationship between MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK and blob count is not explicitly defined' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The assumption 'Builders can accurately estimate their bandwidth capacity and configure the limit appropriately' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Network conditions are stable enough that a static configuration is effective' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Local builders using this feature are honest and not using it to manipulate blob inclusion' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
USER_CONFIGURED_MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK must be a positive integer not exceeding the protocol maximum blob count.
Builders must not use the blob limit configuration to selectively censor specific blob transactions.
After applying the blob limit, the total blob gas in the constructed block must not exceed MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK.
Data received at boundary edge EDGE-EVM-UNTRUSTED-CALL must be validated for correct format and type before processing.
Inputs crossing trust boundary at EDGE-EVM-UNTRUSTED-CALL must be checked for cryptographic validity where applicable.
Data received at boundary edge EDGE-RECEIVE-TX must be validated for correct format and type before processing.
Inputs crossing trust boundary at EDGE-RECEIVE-TX must be checked for cryptographic validity where applicable.

The ambiguity 'The relationship between 'original_value' (value at transaction start) and 'current_value' (present value) in refund calculations is not fully explicit' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'The specification does not explicitly state what happens if a TLOAD reads a key that was never written in the transaction' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.

The ambiguity 'The phrase 'gas remaining' in the stipend check could refer to gas before or after the operation's base cost' must be resolved deterministically: all implementations must adopt an identical interpretation.
The assumption 'The accessed_storage_keys set is assumed to be correctly maintained across all message frames' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'Transient storage is assumed to be completely isolated between transactions' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'An attacker cannot manipulate the static context flag through external means' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
The assumption 'The GAS_CALL_STIPEND check prevents reentrancy exploitation through gas manipulation' must hold. Violation may lead to consensus failure or security degradation.
Transient storage (TLOAD/TSTORE) must be completely cleared at the end of each transaction—no data persists across transactions.
After SSTORE with original_value == current_value == new_value, no gas refund is issued and no state change occurs.
SSTORE in a STATICCALL context must always revert—the static context flag must be checked before any storage write.
The accessed_storage_keys set must be correctly maintained across nested message frames within a transaction.
Before CALL-like operations, the gas remaining must exceed GAS_CALL_STIPEND to prevent reentrancy via gas manipulation.
